item.title: Dielines that survive manufacturing
item.description:
A beautiful mockup can hide fragile structure. Before you fall in love with a render, lock the dieline: panel sizes, glue flaps, grain direction, and bleed.

What to include in a dieline brief

  1. Product dimensions with tolerance (including closure hardware).
  2. Shipping method—air parcel, sea carton, or retail shelf.
  3. Desired open experience—drawer, magnetic flap, sleeve.
  4. Print areas that must remain uninterrupted.

Common failure points

  • Glue flaps too narrow for your board weight
  • Foil or emboss crossing score lines
  • Ignoring caliper when nesting into a mailer

Share your CAD or a clear sketch early. Tendlyn will return a production dieline with notes you can hand to design and ops.

item.title: Designing an unboxing that feels calm
item.description:
Quiet luxury in packaging is not more layers—it is order. Each surface should earn its place in the customer’s hands.

A simple sequence

  1. Outer carton or bag with restrained branding
  2. Sealing sticker that confirms integrity
  3. Tissue with a soft logo
  4. Product nest
  5. Insert card with care or scent notes

Keep fulfillment sane

Every decorative layer costs seconds. We help you choose finishes that photograph beautifully but still pack in a repeatable station layout—critical for DTC reorder volume.

item.title: Choosing materials for scent and beauty goods
item.description:
Fragrance and beauty packaging must balance protection, scent migration, and print fidelity.

Quick material notes

  • Perfume: Rigid boxes with fitted trays; avoid overly porous wraps near alcohol-heavy liquids.
  • Candles: Account for jar weight and heat; soft-touch wraps show scuffs—plan coatings carefully.
  • Cosmetics: Clear labels need high clarity films; tissue should not shed fibers on product.

Export considerations

Humidity and long transit change how adhesives and boards behave. Tell us destination climates early so we can recommend stocks that still look composed on arrival.

item.title: How to Order Custom Printed Boxes: From Artwork to Delivery
item.description:
Preparing custom packaging takes more than a finished logo. Follow the process from selecting box specifications and a dieline to artwork, samples, and delivery.

The tendlyn Team

Published 8/3/2026 • 7 min read

Having a finished logo file is not the same as being ready to place a packaging order. Before artwork can go to print, you need to confirm the packaging structure, dimensions, material, and finishes, then apply your design to a dieline built for those specifications.

item.title: Kraft vs White Custom Mailer Boxes: Which Material Is Right for Your Brand?
item.description:
One substrate adds warmth before you print a single color. The other gives your design nowhere to hide. Here’s how to choose the right one for your mailer box.

The Tendlyn Team
Published 12/1/2024 • 6 min read

The outer surface of a mailer box is the first physical thing a customer touches when an order arrives. Before they read your logo or pull the tape, the material itself already says something about your brand. Choosing between a kraft and white substrate isn’t simply a color preference – it affects how your print looks, how your brand is perceived, and how well the box aligns with your brand’s visual identity. Here’s how to think through that decision clearly.

item.title: Paperboard vs. Corrugated: How to Choose the Right Material for Your Product Box
item.description:
Paperboard delivers polished print and shelf appeal, while corrugated adds shipping strength. Learn when to use each - and when your packaging needs both.

The tendlyn Team
The tendlyn Team
Published 11/12/2025 • 9 min read

Paperboard vs. Corrugated: How to Choose the Right Material for Your Product Box

A folding carton and a corrugated mailer may both be paper-based, but they are engineered for different jobs. Paperboard provides a smooth print surface and a compact format that works well on retail shelves. Corrugated board adds a fluted layer that helps packaging withstand stacking, handling, and shipping.

item.title: Where to Customize Printed Packaging Boxes for Cosmetics and Beauty Brands at Scale
item.description:
Published November 9, 2025 • Reading time: 6 minutes

Cosmetic packaging boxes have to protect fragile products while carrying mandatory label information and presenting product colors accurately both online and in physical stores. Glass bottles, pump dispensers, droppers, detailed ingredient lists, and shade-sensitive artwork all add design constraints that need to be considered before production begins.

tendlyn works with cosmetic and skincare brands on orders ranging from initial low-volume runs to hundreds of thousands of units. Common procurement questions include how much panel space the required text will take up, which finishing technique best matches the brand positioning, and what a sensible order quantity looks like for an unproven SKU. This guide covers what beauty brands should confirm before requesting packaging quotes.
